newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast cocoa shipments to N.America soar.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast cocoa shipments to N.America soar.

text.p: Ivory Coast cocoa bean shipments routed directly to the North America jumped tenfold in the first 11 months of 1995/96 as shippers took advantage of government liberalisation of shipping rates last year, exporters said.
Europe remained the main destination, with cumulative October-August shipments to the Netherlands reaching 431,243 tonnes, up from 369,412 in the same 1994/95 period, port authority figures show.
But exports to North America were 205,132 tonnes, against 20,062 for the same period of 1994/95.
"(Shipping) rates for the coming year could be even lower and if that is the case we will certainly see a further rise," said one large exporter.
August exports dwindled ahead of the new main crop season expected to open in early October. North America took 1,015 tonnes against 863 tonnes for the Netherlands.

Trade sources said the overall jump in exports to North America was mainly due to a decision by Ivory Coast's Caistab marketing board to modify the c.i.f. bareme governing shipping rates to North America at the start of this season and the shipping companies' agreement to lower their charges.
This, they added, made it cost effective to ship cocoa there directly rather than sending it via Amsterdam.
The old bareme rates were Kept artificially high to protect the former national line Sitram.
Dutch warehousing sources say they have had their best year ever as cocoa has poured into Amsterdam to be delivered against the squeezed September contract in London.
Ivory Coast's 1995/96 crop is put at a record 1.2 million tonnes, about a third more than the previous best crop in 1994/95.
